assessmentPlan: Only prospective cumulative 128/512-pair looks. Existing SR-024 paired-normal rule with family alpha .05/2^contrastIndex, Bonferroni across looks, minimum 20 pairs on each side, 2.5-SE sensitivity, bounded-pair reporting and nonbinding computational futility. No block looks, post-close extension, retuning or selective replay. Explicit owner acceptance remains separate.

selectionRationale: Select completed-hint policy 4 against the unchanged accepted champion in the one-worker EFFORT domain. It scored 30 W / 19 D / 15 L (+82.97 Elo) in the complete development screen; the combined policy 7 scored +60.31 Elo with broad correlated uncertainty. Direct conditional contrasts scored +5.43 Elo for retention and +10.86 Elo for the nominal-learning filter, both with wide intervals crossing zero. These do not reject O2 or require individual significance for a combination. Policy 4 has the clearer availability hypothesis, less additional mutable state, and lower observed fixed-depth elapsed cost (0.894 of champion versus 0.908 for policy 7). Its history remains the accepted baseline. Choose this complete configuration for fresh confirmation, retain policy 7 and the O2 controls as viable but unconfirmed alternatives, and avoid a parameter/configuration sweep without a new decision-relevant hypothesis. All semantic/ownership/oracle checks passed; development estimates remain selection-biased.

confirmationForecast.interpretation: Plug-in forecasts from selected development data, not guaranteed power. Six losing pairs out of 32 imply 24 below-half pairs at 128 in expectation; normal eligibility still is not guaranteed. The inherited bounded rule applies if the normal rule is ineligible. At 512 pairs the required score half-width is about 0.031, roughly 22 Elo locally. No small-gain power claim. Add roughly 5-10% preflight/session overhead. Admit complete blocks in bounded resource windows, initially through the first 128-pair scheduled look only. Operational pauses are not statistical looks. Continue only according to the predeclared statistical rule and available non-disruptive workstation capacity. One game at a time, one Search worker, BelowNormal, 512 MiB heap per engine. Preserve all host observations; no automatic disruptive 12-hour run.
